cs.t: my two seagate drives in my nas failed, one in 09/16 and one 01/17. thank god for raid. i replaced them with bigger seagate drives. maybee i should not.

I highly recommend Synology. QNAP and FreeNAS seem really great in a lot of ways, but Synology is the solution for people who want something solid that takes up as little of their time as possible. Avoid Drobo and Seagate. I would make your first / boot drive a SSD, and put WD Reds in the rest, 2 drive redundancy if you want to be super safe. In addition, I recommend using the built-in cloud backup software to backup high-value data to Blackblaze B2. Happy to answer any other questions.

cs.t: >WD mixed both CMR and SMR I  was  a fan of WD HDDs before and I was in the market for some drives for my new NAS a few years ago. When I checked what drives were on the market, I saw WD doing that while Seagate still clearly marked which drives were which. I swore off WD that day because my time is too valuable for their bullshit. I have no clue if they have amended their marketing, but I don't care since as far as I'm aware Seagate still clearly marks them and the drives I bought from them have all been fine. I'll likely buy Seagate again next time I'm in the market.
